text:
tariq: hey all, day 1 q about where to store Redwood keys when using VSCode + GitHub Codespaces. i've been using a global .env in my home dir but worried about leaks when i push dotfiles. any recommended local-only patterns for new hires?
jen: welcome! :wave: never keep keys in dotfiles. recommended patterns: 1) use OS keyring (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / libsecret on linux) and a small helper that injects env at runtime; 2) use SecretsManager + per-repo service token for CI/Codespaces; 3) for quick local work use sandbox keys copied into a gitignored .env.local.
tariq: for Codespaces specifically, is it ok to set the secret in repo settings so Codespaces gets it automatically?
devex-bot: docs: https://internal.redwood.devex/keys-and-quotas  see "Codespaces & Cloud Dev Envs". Pattern: store token as a repo secret (scoped to the org/repo), enable it for Codespaces, and restrict who can create Codespaces. For demos, prefer ephemeral tokens.
chris: security add-on: if you store a token in a repo secret, enable least privilege and rotate often. For personal dev, put keys in your local OS keychain and use environment injection, or use the dev-tools helper (rw-secret-load) which reads from keychain and writes to process env for the session. Example (mac):
```
# add:
security add-generic-password -a $USER -s redwood_sandbox -w "$SANDBOX_KEY"
# load:
export RW_KEY=$(security find-generic-password -s redwood_sandbox -w)
```
tariq: sweet. how do Codespaces and GitHub Actions quotas differ from local sandbox? will i see 429s differently?
jen: sandbox in Codespaces still counts against the same sandbox rate limits. Codespaces often share egress IPs, so you may hit concurrent limits faster. For CI/Actions, use per-repo service tokens and gate heavy jobs by checking X-RateLimit-Remaining or GET /v1/account/limits. If you expect bursts in Codespaces for a workshop, request a temporary hosted dev key with IP restrictions or ephemeral tokens minted by your workshop backend.
pip: small snippet for dev-tools helper (bash) to avoid committing keys:
```
# .devcontainer/postStartCommand
if [ -n "$CODESPACE_NAME" ]; then
  export RW_KEY=$(gh secret -R myorg/myrepo view RW_SANDBOX_KEY -s)
fi
```
(We recommend using the GitHub CLI with repo-level secrets access, not checked-in files.)
tariq: last question: can I programmatically check remaining quota from Codespaces before running a local script so it doesn't spam the sandbox?
devex-bot: yes: check response headers for X-RateLimit-Remaining or call GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/limits. Example curl: `curl -sI -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | grep X-RateLimit-Remaining` Use that to gate heavy runs.
tariq: thanks everyone, i'll move keys to my keychain and wire up the Codespaces secret for repo-only use. will open a temporary hosted key request if we need more concurrency for demos. :thumbsup:
